id: 556-第一次蒂卡爾-卡拉科爾戰爭
theater: 佩滕盆地蒂卡爾至卡拉科爾

battle.name: 第一次蒂卡爾-卡拉科爾戰爭
battle.theater: 佩滕盆地蒂卡爾至卡拉科爾
battle.brief: 公元556年，佩滕盆地霸主蒂卡爾在王克伊尼奇約納爾阿赫一世治下打出一場斧戰，進攻佩滕東南扼住南去山道的中繼城邦卡拉科爾，想把被卡拉克穆爾攻破後散掉的附庸重新收攏。戰事靠聯盟倒戈與縱火破壞，最後沒能拆掉北方同盟，反而替五年後那場星戰鋪了路。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 第一次蒂卡爾-卡拉科爾戰爭爆發於公元556年，是瑪雅古典期佩滕盆地城邦政治的一次正面較量。交戰一方是蒂卡爾：這座城邦在佩滕伊察湖以北的沼澤低地建起巨型台形建築群與長紀年碑銘，自稱「第一穆塔爾」，王號作 kaloomteʼ「大王」，是六世紀上半葉中部瑪雅低地的霸主，靠附庸與盟城網絡控制周邊交通。另一方是卡拉科爾：佩滕東南、貝里斯境內扼住通往南部山地的中繼城邦，有自己的球場、自己的陶器風格與自己的大王名號，並且跟北方的卡拉克穆爾（貝利茲的蛇族王國）往來密切。第三方是卡拉克穆爾，它在537年攻破蒂卡爾之後一直覬覦低地。三方都沒有常備軍：出征的是王室核心圈的人——王子、祭司與親信——加上按村社編組的民兵，武器自帶，乾糧按戶供應，糧食是玉米、豆、南瓜、可可與鹽。指揮極簡，通常只設一名統帥在陣前，勝負由城邦聯盟的穩定度與儀式程序能否完成決定。
countriesEn: The First Tikal-Calakal War broke out in 556 CE, a direct trial of strength between the city-states of the Classic Maya lowlands. One side was Tikal: the city had raised its vast pyramidal complexes and its Long Count monuments on the swampy lowland north of Lake Petén Itzá, called itself the First Mutal, gave its king the title kaloomteʼ, the great lord, and stood as the dominant power of the central Maya lowland in the first half of the sixth century, holding the surrounding towns through a web of vassals and allies. The other side was Calakal, an intermediate city-state in southeastern Petén inside modern Belize that guarded the road into the southern highlands, with its own ballcourt, its own ceramic style and its own great lord, and with close ties to Calakmul to the north, the Snake dynasty state in the Belize valley. The third party was Calakmul itself, which had destroyed Tikal in 537 and had coveted the lowland ever since. None of the three had standing armies: what marched out were the households of the royal core, princes, priests and favourites, together with militia raised village by village, weapons carried by the men themselves and dry rations collected household by household, maize, beans, squash, cacao and salt. Command was simple; usually a single commander stood at the head of the column, and the outcome was decided by the stability of the inter-city alliance and by whether the ritual programme could be carried through.
people: 留下姓名的當事人不多，能確定的更少。蒂卡爾方面，此役的統帥是蒂卡爾王克伊尼奇約納爾阿赫一世（K'inich Yo'nal Ahk I，約511至567年在位），他是把蒂卡爾在537年崩解之後重新立住王權、重新立碑的人物，也是六世紀初那種由「蒂卡爾夫人」與卡洛姆泰巴赫蘭、鳥爪共同執政的分享王權之後的第一位獨自執政的君主，這一點對戰爭中的權威來源很重要。卡拉科爾方面，留下來的是銘文而不是完整人名：其大王沿用 kaloomteʼ 名號，而記載這場敗仗的關鍵物證卡拉科爾二十一號祭壇殘損嚴重，人物名至今無法完整釋讀；「持燧石者」特卡布查克（Te' K'ab Chaak）這個名字在學界多繫於卡拉克穆爾一系，落到卡拉科爾頭上時身分仍有爭議。五六年後被聯軍擒獲的那位蒂卡爾國王「雙鳥」（Wak Chan K'awiil），名字正是靠卡拉科爾二十一號祭壇的殘文才被保存下來。研究這場戰爭的依靠，是賓夕法尼亞大學蒂卡爾計畫的《蒂卡爾報告》系列、貝利茲的卡拉克穆爾考古計畫的發掘報告，以及馬丁與格魯貝的《瑪雅象形文字辭典》一類工具書。
peopleEn: Those who left a name are few, and those whose identity can be fixed are fewer still. On the Tikal side the commander of this war was the ruler K'inich Yo'nal Ahk I, who reigned roughly from 511 to 567 CE; he was the king who set royal authority on its feet again after the collapse of 537 and who brought the monument tradition back to life at Tikal, and he was the first ruler to govern alone after the sharing of power characteristic of the early sixth century, when the so-called Tikal Lady governed alongside Kaloomteʼ Bahlam and Bird Claw, a point that matters for where authority came from in this war. On the Calakal side what survives is inscription rather than a complete personal name: its lord still bore the title kaloomteʼ, and the key physical witness to the defeat, Altar 21 at Calakal, is so badly damaged that the name of the man has never been fully read; the name Te' K'ab Chaak, he of the flint, is tied by most scholars to the Calakmul line, and its attachment to Calakal remains disputed. The Tikal king captured five years later, the Double Bird (Wak Chan K'awiil), is known to us only because the broken text of Altar 21 at Calakal preserved his name. The scholarship on this war rests on the series of Tikal Reports from the University of Pennsylvania's Tikal Project, on the excavation reports of the Calakmul archaeological project in Belize, and on tools such as the Maya Hieroglyphic Dictionary of Martin and Grube.
kits: 先說卡面：這是一把亞述長矛，標示年代為公元前九百年前後，是新亞述帝國步兵的制式裝備——短柄、長刃、配著鐵鏃，亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。這件兵器從未到過中美洲，佩滕盆地的瑪雅戰士手裡從來沒有這種短柄長刃鐵矛；本站的卡片是拿文明原型兵器配史實戰役，這一點必須老老實實講清楚。瑪雅戰場上同位置、同功能的是長桿突刺矛：硬木杆，綁上削尖的燧石、灰燼石或蛋白石葉形矛頭，以繩索、樹脂或皮條紮緊，長度多在兩至三公尺，既能刺穿人體與鎧甲縫隙，也能在投擲前當握柄支撐；另有投矛器（atlatl）及其鏃，射程約一百米上下。輔戰武器包括鑲嵌黑曜石刀片的木棒（學界沿用 macuahuitl 一名）、彈弓、石錘，以及銅斧或石斧；防護是木條骨架外蒙獸皮或棉布的圓形與矩形盾牌，另有棉絮甲、繃布頭盔，精英戰士再添羽飾頭盔、翡翠與貝殼頸飾。攻城沒有投石機、撞車或雲梯，摧毀建築靠縱火——硬木梁架加棕櫚與茅草的殿宇一點就著；遠射靠投矛器與彈弓，古典期低地並無常規的弓箭配備。運輸與補給用獨木舟、舟身拖曳、馱獸與人力背負，糧食是玉米、豆、南瓜、可可與鹽，沿石砌堤道與沼澤小徑運送。
kitsEn: First the card: this is an Assyrian spear, dated to around 900 BC, standard equipment of the infantry of the Neo-Assyrian Empire, a short shaft with a long blade and an iron head, tied by the Assyrians together with the bow and ironwork as one riverine city after another fell. This weapon never reached Mesoamerica, and no Maya warrior in Petén ever held a short-shafted long-bladed iron spear; the cards on this site set a prototype weapon of one civilisation beside a real battle, and that has to be said plainly. What stood in the same place and did the same work on a Maya battlefield was the long thrusting spear: a hardwood shaft with a leaf-shaped point of chipped flint, chert or obsidian, lashed on with cord, resin or hide thong, two to three metres long, usable both to stab through the gaps of a body and to serve as a support before the throw. There were also the atlatl and its darts, thrown to a range of around a hundred metres, and the auxiliaries: wooden clubs inset with obsidian blades, which scholarship still calls macuahuitl, slings, stone hammers, and copper or stone axes. Protection consisted of round and rectangular shields of wooden staves covered with hide or cloth, together with cotton-padded armour and cloth-wrapped helmets, while elite warriors added feathered headdresses, jade and shell necklaces. There were no siege engines, no battering rams and no ladders; buildings were destroyed by fire, since a hall of hardwood frames roofed with palm and thatch caught at once, and long range was worked with the atlatl and the sling rather than with any regular archery. Transport and supply used dugout canoes, canoe haulage, pack animals and human porters, and the food was maize, beans, squash, cacao and salt, moved along the stone causeways and the swamp paths.
tactics: 瑪雅人沒有攻城塔，也沒有撞車，對付台形建築群只有三招：一是切斷城邦之間的白石堤道（sacbe），在雨季與沼澤地帶尤其致命；二是以投矛器與彈弓從遠處向台基、屋脊與廣場傾瀉投射物，同時放火燒掉硬木搭成的殿宇，逼迫守軍在煙與碎片之間失去指揮，然後沿石階攀上台頂，在狹窄平台上展開近身格鬥；三是派出小股隊伍切斷對方的糧道與取水點。聯盟外交先於會戰：蒂卡爾與卡拉科爾各自經營互不重疊的附庸網絡，把對手的盟友逐個拉過來，聯盟一旦倒戈，戰局整體傾斜。行軍多在旱季（佩滕一帶約在十月至翌年五月），以便穿越沼澤、濕地與雨林，六月以後雨季不宜遠征，這也是碑銘上的出征多集中在旱季末段的原因。戰鬥以步兵核心展開：矛手與持矛手列於前列互相試探，投矛手與彈弓手在兩翼及後方覆蓋，短兵相接後勝負多由體力、紀律與地形決定。奪城之後不大肆劫掠，勝方通常摧毀碑銘、砸損公共雕塑以象徵性展示戰果，並在儀式上處置被俘的國王。防守一方靠的是五世紀修築的環繞約一百二十平方公里的壕溝與土垣、蓄水池，以及跨越沼澤的堤道，作為進退與補給的通道。
tacticsEn: The Maya had no siege towers and no battering rams, and against a pyramidal complex they had three means: to cut the white causeways (sacbe) that linked city to city, which was devastating in the wet season and among the swamps; to pour javelins and sling-stones from a distance onto the platforms, the roof ridges and the plazas, and at the same time set fire to the halls built of hardwood, so that the defenders lost command amid smoke and falling debris, and then to climb the stone stairways onto the narrow platforms and fight it out at close quarters; and to send small parties to cut the enemy's food route and water points. Allied diplomacy came before the field battle: Tikal and Calakal each ran a network of vassals that did not overlap the other's, and pulled the opponent's partners over one by one, so that when an alliance flipped the whole war tilted. Campaigns were fought in the dry season, roughly October to May in Petén, so that the columns could cross swamp, wetland and rainforest; after June the rains made long marches impossible, which is why the campaigns named in the inscriptions cluster at the end of the dry season. The fighting was decided by infantry: spearmen and shield bearers probed each other in the front, dart throwers and slingers covered the flanks and the rear, and once the sides closed, the result turned on endurance, discipline and ground. A captured city was not generally looted; the victors normally smashed the monuments and damaged the public sculpture to display the outcome symbolically, and disposed of the captive king in ritual. The defenders relied on the ditch and earthwork system built in the fifth century around some 120 square kilometres, on the reservoirs, and on the causeways that crossed the swamps, as routes of entry, retreat and supply.
data: 可核對的數字集中在幾處。年代：戰爭列表把此戰定在公元556年；瑪雅長紀年曆的9.6世代約相當於公元556至572年，562年那場決戰記在9.6.8.4.2，由此往回推六年，556年大致落在9.6.3世代前後。距離：蒂卡爾至卡拉科爾直線約二十公里，實際行軍要繞過沼澤與河道；蒂卡爾至卡拉克穆爾約一百公里。蒂卡爾本體：遺址總面積逾十六平方公里，含約三千座建築，主要建築群約二點五平方公里，國家公園保護面積約五萬七千公頃；核心區人口在七世紀前後約一萬人，周邊約五萬人；年降雨量約一千九百四十五毫米，全城僅靠十座蓄水池儲水；五世紀修築的壕溝與土垣環繞約一百二十平方公里。卡拉科爾與卡拉克穆爾的城邦範圍約二百平方公里，卡拉克穆爾最後一次有紀年事件是10.1.10.0.0，即公元859年。關鍵節點：562年之後蒂卡爾進入約一百二十年的中斷期，直到682年才重新出現有紀年的紀念碑。兵力、俘虜數與傷亡，銘文從不記數目，只記擒獲、焚燒與占領，所以任何精確的兵員數都是後人推估，不能當作事實。月份方面，現存銘文只把此戰定位在9.6世代之內，具體月令無從考定，卡片的月份欄按年初計，並非出於史料記載。
dataEn: The checkable figures cluster in a few places. Date: the war lists place this war in 556 CE, and the 9.6 cycle of the Maya Long Count corresponds broadly to 556 to 572 CE; the decisive battle of 562 is dated 9.6.8.4.2, and six years back from that puts 556 in the neighbourhood of the 9.6.3 cycle. Distance: Tikal to Calakal is about twenty kilometres as the crow flies, though the route had to bend around swamp and watercourses, and Tikal to Calakmul about a hundred kilometres. Tikal itself: the site covers more than sixteen square kilometres with roughly three thousand buildings, the principal architectural group some two and a half square kilometres, and the national park protecting it about fifty-seven thousand hectares; the population of the core was around ten thousand in the seventh century and some fifty thousand in its hinterland; annual rainfall was about 1,945 millimetres and the whole city relied on ten reservoirs for water; the ditch and earthwork system of the fifth century enclosed some 120 square kilometres. The territories of Calakal and Calakmul were about two hundred square kilometres, and the last dated event at Calakmul is 10.1.10.0.0, that is 859 CE. Key markers: after 562 Tikal entered a hiatus of about 120 years and did not raise a dated monument again until 682. Numbers of men, of prisoners and of casualties are never given, for the inscriptions record only captures, burnings and occupations; every exact figure for the size of the armies is a modern estimate and cannot be treated as fact. As to the month, the surviving inscriptions place the war only within the 9.6 cycle and no month can be established; the month field of this card is set at the beginning of the year as a convention and does not rest on the sources.
cause: 打起來的理由有三層。最外一層是地位：蒂卡爾在537年被卡拉克穆爾攻破之後，低地霸權受挫，附庸網絡鬆動，作為佩滕核心的宗教與政治正統卻仍在，於是急需一場勝利來把散掉的附庸重新收攏、把自立的邊境城邦壓回從屬的位置。卡拉科爾正是這樣的一個城邦：它扼住佩滕東南通往南部山地的要道，握有可可、蜂鳥羽毛、翡翠、貝殼與通往科潘一線的物資通道，不願長期充當附庸，又與北方蛇族王國卡拉克穆爾在語言、信仰與貿易上同氣連枝。裡面一層是生態與經濟：古典期低地人口膨脹，燒荒與過度取水壓縮了可用農地，蒂卡爾一帶的彎曲河道全靠堤壩與蓄水塘調節，誰控制水源，誰就控制城邦的存亡。最內一層是儀式合法性：蒂卡爾的斧戰（ch'ak）是征服性戰爭，勝方要戴上敗者的頭飾以示佔有，而星戰則把金星吉凶掛在出征上，兩者都要求勝者先把敵方從宇宙秩序裡抹去。五五六年這次出手，本質是把叛離的邊境城邦重新收回秩序的一次嘗試。
causeEn: There are three layers of reason behind the fighting. The outermost is status. After Calakmul destroyed Tikal in 537 the lowland hegemony had been dented and the network of vassals had loosened, but the religious and political orthodoxy of the Petén core still stood, and a victory was needed to gather the scattered vassals back in and to push the self-governing border towns back into subjection. Calakal was exactly such a town: it held the road from southeastern Petén into the southern highlands and controlled the material flows of cacao, hummingbird feathers, jade, shell and the line toward Copán, and it had no wish to remain a vassal for long, being linked to the northern Snake dynasty of Calakmul in language, in cult and in trade. Inside that lies ecology and economy: the population of the lowlands expanded in the Classic period, slash-and-burn and over-drawing of water compressed the farmland available, and the winding channels around Tikal could be regulated only by dams and reservoirs, so that whoever held the water held the survival of the city-states. At the centre lies ritual legitimacy: the ch'ak, the axe war, was a war of conquest whose victor took the headband of the defeated as a sign of possession, while the star war tied the campaign to the auspices of Venus, and both forms required the enemy to be struck out of the order of things first. The expedition of 556 was in essence an attempt to draw a seceded border town back into that order.
impact: 這場戰爭的影響，主要不體現在蒂卡爾當年的勝負，而體現在它之後的走向。對蒂卡爾而言，556年出兵說明舊秩序仍有收攏力，也說明佩滕的權力競爭並沒有因為537年的焚燒而結束；但這一役把蒂卡爾的軍力與注意力又一次投到南線，核心防備空出，五年後的星戰才有可乘之機。對卡拉科爾而言，這一戰沒有帶來滅亡，反而保住城邦、擴大影響，並在北線找到卡拉克穆爾這個可靠的同盟者，聯盟從此成為牠在佩滕生存的主要倚仗。對整個中部瑪雅低地，562至738年是權力重心西移的時期：卡拉克穆爾獨佔低地，蒂卡爾沉寂，直到695年蒂卡爾在雙月卡威爾二世治下扭轉戰局，738年的聯軍之役更讓卡拉克穆爾一蹶不振。學術上，562年事件被定為早古典期與晚古典期的分水嶺，蒂卡爾約一百二十年的中斷期從此成為分期與城市衰變研究的基本坐標。星戰這種把天文曆法與戰爭綁在一起的形式也自此傳開，往後數百年一再被引用，直到後古典期仍作為王權正統的來源。
impactEn: The effect of this war shows less in Tikal's fortunes in the year itself than in what followed. For Tikal, the campaign of 556 showed that the old order could still gather people in, and also that the competition for power in Petén had not ended with the burning of 537; but it also put Tikal's troops and attention on the southern front once more, leaving the core thinly defended, and that is what the star war of five years later was able to take advantage of. For Calakal the war brought no destruction: it preserved the city, enlarged its influence, and pushed it deeper towards Calakmul, which it now used as a reliable northern partner, and the alliance became the main prop of its survival in Petén. For the central Maya lowland as a whole, 562 to 738 was the period in which the centre of gravity moved west; Calakmul dominated the lowland while Tikal lay dormant, until in 695 Tikal under the Double Moon, K'awiil II, reversed the situation, and the allied campaign of 738 finished Calakmul off. Academically, the event of 562 has been taken as the watershed between the Early and Late Classic periods, and the hiatus of roughly 120 years at Tikal has become a basic coordinate for studies of periodisation and of urban decline. The star war, the form that binds an astronomical calendar to a war, spread from that point and was cited again and again for centuries afterwards, serving even into the Postclassic as a source of royal legitimacy.
result: 就現有材料而言，第一次蒂卡爾-卡拉科爾戰爭的結局屬於「沒有輸家、也沒有贏家」的那種：蒂卡爾並未攻下卡拉科爾，也沒有摧毀北方的卡拉克穆爾-卡拉科爾同盟；卡拉科爾也沒有被從地圖上抹去，蒂卡爾的低地霸權仍在延續。真正發生的是兩件事：一是蒂卡爾把一部分附庸與物資通道重新收攏在自己手裡，暫時穩住了537年之後的真空；二是這場勝利把卡拉科爾更深地推向卡拉克穆爾，使兩個佩滕以外的勢力結成一體，並給了它們在五年內完成兵力與糧秣積蓄的時間。結果是五年後的562年四月，卡拉克穆爾與卡拉科爾聯軍以第一次星戰的形式打進蒂卡爾，國王被擒並在儀式上處置，城市沒有遭到全面劫掠，制度卻被折斷：蒂卡爾不再豎碑，公共雕塑被有意毀損，進入約一百二十年的中斷期。從兵器角度看，這一場戰爭再一次說明長桿突刺矛在古典瑪雅軍中的位置——它不是攻城武器，而是列陣、衝鋒與守壘的骨幹；卡面所繪的亞述短柄長刃鐵矛，屬於另一個世界近東的技術譜系，從未出現在中美洲，與瑪雅綁在硬木杆上的燧石矛同為「尖頭綁柄」的長矛家族，卻分屬兩個互不相通的技術史。
resultEn: On the material that survives, the outcome of the First Tikal-Calakal War is of the kind that produces neither a loser nor a winner. Tikal did not take Calakal, and it did not break up the northern Calakmul-Calakal alliance; Calakal was not struck from the map either, and Tikal's lowland hegemony continued. Two things did happen. First, Tikal drew a portion of its vassals and its material routes back into its own hands and steadied the vacuum that had opened in 537 for a time. Second, that victory pushed Calakal deeper into Calakmul, fused two powers from beyond Petén into one, and gave them the time to build up troops and supplies over the following five years. The result came in April 562, when the allied army of Calakmul and Calakal entered Tikal in the form of the first star war: the king was taken and disposed of in ritual, the city was not comprehensively looted, but the institution was broken, for Tikal raised no more monuments, its public sculpture was deliberately smashed, and the hiatus of some 120 years began. As for the weapons, this war once again sets out the place of the long thrusting spear in the Classic Maya army: it was not an engine of siege, but the backbone of the line, of the charge and of the defence of the platform. The short-shafted long-bladed iron spear drawn on the card belongs to the technological lineage of the ancient Near East and never set foot in Mesoamerica; it shares with the Maya flint spear lashed to a hardwood shaft membership in the family of shaft-and-pointed-head spears, yet the two belong to technical histories that never touched.
